items.title: New No Surprises Act rules force employer plans to justify claim cuts - benefitspro.com
items.reason: This item directly addresses new No Surprises Act rules affecting claim denials and justification requirements, which is a concrete regulatory development impacting how employer plans implement the law's requirements.
items.summary: New No Surprises Act rules require employer plans to provide detailed justifications when cutting or denying claims, strengthening transparency and accountability in the claims process. This regulatory development, emerging from HHS/CMS implementation of the No Surprises Act, directly affects how self-insured employer health plans must handle claim determinations and communicate denials to beneficiaries. Revenue-cycle teams must update claim denial and appeal processes to comply with enhanced documentation requirements, potentially increasing administrative burden but reducing dispute resolution complications. The rules reinforce the Act's balance-billing protections by ensuring plans cannot cut claims without substantive reasoning, directly impacting claim adjudication workflows and IDR exposure.
